subject: Handshake criteria & acceptance exercises for HealX evaluation
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@healx.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healx.com, eng-team@healx.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Handshake criteria & acceptance exercises for HealX evaluation

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we discussed, HealX wants an explicit mutual action plan so procurement and engineering can sign off on the four-week evaluation. Attached is a first-pass MAP (healx_map_draft.xlsx) with proposed milestones. High-level asks from our side:

- Duration: 4 weeks (integration, smoke, burn-in/stability, handoff)
- Success definition: a short, measurable checklist we can use to greenlight a later pilot
- Exit gates: clear pass/fail criteria for the evaluation to avoid ambiguity at close
- Acceptance exercises: sample vignettes and tests we will run (functional + safety)

To get the ball rolling, here are our suggested metrics (we can refine):
- Latency: P95 generation latency < 150 ms (for 512-token prompts)
- Throughput: sustained 120 req/s for inference endpoints during load test
- Quality: entity extraction F1 >= 0.85 on our sample set (closed domain)
- Hallucination floor: < 2% of outputs with factual hallucination on spot-checks
- Cost target: average token cost per 1k tokens <= our budget threshold we will share offline
- Security/compliance: audit log exports available and data retention window set to 30 days

Acceptance exercises we need in the MAP (examples):
1) Clinical note summarization: 250 notes -> check recall & hallucination vignettes
2) ICD mapping: 500 mapping pairs -> accuracy + top-1/top-3 checks
3) PII redaction: injected PHI snippets -> verify redaction and audit trail
4) Adversarial prompts: 50 edge cases to validate guardrails

Can you confirm these as a starting point and map owners for each acceptance exercise? Also confirm the SOW timeline — procurement will need explicit exit conditions to cut the PO. I’ve attached the MAP draft.

– Sam
Senior Product Manager, HealX

Attachment: healx_map_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@healx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:16:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Handshake criteria & acceptance exercises for HealX evaluation

Sam —

Appreciate the clear list. This is exactly the kind of MAP detail that helps speed procurement. A few notes from our side after an internal huddle:

- High-level timeline looks good (we agree on 4 weeks). We propose a slightly modified week breakdown:
  • Week 0 (pre-integration): SSO/keys & test data ingress + baseline smoke tests
  • Week 1: integration + low-volume validation (vignettes 1&3)
  • Week 2: functional acceptance + adversarial vignettes (2 & 4)
  • Week 3: stability burn-in (scale to target QPS) + cost sampling
  • Week 4: handoff + post-eval report and decision window

- Technical acceptance additions we recommend:
  • KV cache hit-rate target: >= 75% for repeated conversation flows (reduces per-token cost)
  • Tail-latency SLA: P99 < 400 ms as fall-through (monitored in Redwood Console)
  • Error-rate guardrail: 5xxs < 0.5% during any 15m window during load test

- Acceptance exercises: we’ll author a short doc (redwood_acceptance_vignettes.pdf) with explicit input/output checks + pass/fail thresholds. We’ll also include synthetic adversarial variations to stress guardrails.

- Escape hatch / rollback plan: if any critical acceptance test fails (quality or security), we will immediately scale down traffic to a read-only baseline (your pre-eval model) and open a 48-hour remediation window. If remediation fails, the eval is considered failed and procurement can pause the PO.

Ownership suggestion:
  • HealX owns ICD mapping dataset & labeling (Sam)
  • Redwood owns vignettes authoring, load harness, and monitoring (Jonas/Karthik)
  • Joint review for PII redaction results (Lauren to coordinate)

I’ve attached our acceptance vignette doc — it has the initial checks and sample pass/fail assertions. Can you confirm owners and whether procurement needs any additional artifacts for the PO?

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_acceptance_vignettes.pdf (doc, 28KB)

Subject: Internal: Canary & monitoring notes for HealX eval (RWF-9382)

Folks —

Quick technical rundown that should be added into the MAP under runbook:

- Canary plan: 3-stage ramp during Week 3 (1% -> 10% -> 100% target QPS) with 30m stability checks between stages. If error-rate > 0.3% or P99 spikes > 2x baseline at any stage, abort and revert to previous stage.

- Monitoring: Wire up the following Redwood Console dashboards prior to Week 1 integration:
  • Per-route token usage & cost sampling
  • Tail latency (P50/P95/P99) with per-model breakdown
  • Trace sampling for 5xx errors and hallucination spot-checks (attachments will include sample trace format)

- Acceptance test automation: We should provide a scripts folder in the shared Drive with a single-command runner that executes the 4 acceptance exercises and outputs pass/fail + artifact tarball for procurement. That artifact is what procurement will attach to the PO.

- Test-data handling: Ensure data minimization — for PII redaction vignettes use pseudonymized samples. HealX needs to confirm if we can use synthetic variants for public smoke tests.

I’ll draft the runbook and drop it in the MAP folder by EOD tomorrow.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
